label: Herniated intervertebral disc
recognitionCue: Radicular/spinal symptoms with a myelographic filling defect
structureMechanism: Disc material narrows/indents the contrast-filled subarachnoid contour
discriminator: Myelography can reveal disc anomaly; deck gives no syndrome-level presentation
visualSuggestion: Cord, roots, thecal sac, protruding disc

label: Spinal tumor
recognitionCue: Mass altering the subarachnoid outline on myelography
structureMechanism: Space-occupying lesion around cord/roots
discriminator: Irregular contrast column rather than normal smooth outline
visualSuggestion: Myelogram column with focal block

label: Angiography-induced cerebral infarction
recognitionCue: New focal deficit after catheter angiography
structureMechanism: Arterial spasm reduces cerebral perfusion
discriminator: Iatrogenic timing after angiography
visualSuggestion: Catheter -> arterial spasm -> infarct

label: Cerebral angioma / arteriovenous malformation
recognitionCue: Abnormal vascular tangle on angiography; presentation not specified
structureMechanism: Direct artery-vein vascular malformation
discriminator: Angiographic nidus/tangle rather than a simple focal dilation
visualSuggestion: Feeding artery -> nidus -> draining vein

label: Intracranial aneurysm
recognitionCue: Focal vascular outpouching on angiography; presentation not specified
structureMechanism: Weak arterial wall dilates
discriminator: Focal sac/outpouching versus stenosis or AVM
visualSuggestion: Circle of Willis with berry-like pouch

label: Cerebral arterial stenosis/obstruction
recognitionCue: Narrowed or interrupted vessel on angiography
structureMechanism: Reduced lumen limits distal perfusion
discriminator: Narrowing/occlusion rather than hemorrhagic density
visualSuggestion: Normal vessel beside narrowed vessel

label: Cerebral infarction
recognitionCue: Acute focal neurologic deficit; early noncontrast CT can still be normal
structureMechanism: Ischemic tissue injury
discriminator: CT is often obtained first to exclude hemorrhage; MRI can show infarct
visualSuggestion: CT timeline: early normal -> later hypodensity

label: Brain tumor
recognitionCue: Progressive focal/ICP symptoms; contrast-enhancing boundary
structureMechanism: BBB disruption allows contrast enhancement around tumor
discriminator: Contrast T1 shows boundaries; T2 highlights surrounding inflammatory/edematous reaction
visualSuggestion: Tumor core, enhancing rim, surrounding edema

label: Increased intracranial pressure
recognitionCue: Headache/vomiting/papilledema; CT before lumbar puncture
structureMechanism: Space/volume increase raises pressure
discriminator: Imaging precedes LP when raised ICP is suspected
visualSuggestion: Skull volume compartments and pressure arrow

label: Epidural hemorrhage
recognitionCue: Head trauma with a biconvex/lenticular extra-axial collection
structureMechanism: Skull fracture damages a dural/meningeal vessel
discriminator: Lens-shaped blood
visualSuggestion: Skull-dura plane and lenticular CT shape

label: Subarachnoid hemorrhage
recognitionCue: Blood tracking through CSF spaces/sulci on CT; thunderclap headache
structureMechanism: Bleeding into subarachnoid space
discriminator: Follows cisterns/sulci rather than forming a lens/crescent
visualSuggestion: Circle of Willis and basal cistern blood

label: Subdural hemorrhage
recognitionCue: Trauma with crescent-shaped collection
structureMechanism: Tearing of small traversing/bridging veins
discriminator: Crescent crosses sutures; contrasts with lenticular epidural
visualSuggestion: Bridging vein from cortex to sinus

label: Multiple sclerosis
recognitionCue: Periventricular lesions, better seen with FLAIR
structureMechanism: CNS demyelinating plaques
discriminator: Periventricular distribution and CSF suppression on FLAIR
visualSuggestion: Ventricles with radial white-matter plaques

label: CNS disease in AIDS
recognitionCue: T2-sensitive CNS pathology; specific entity/presentation not given
structureMechanism: Not specified in deck
discriminator: Do not invent an AIDS diagnosis from this example
visualSuggestion: T2 image with label only

label: Brain abscess
recognitionCue: T2-sensitive lesion; fever/focal deficit
structureMechanism: Localized infection with inflammatory edema
discriminator: Infection context; deck does not provide ring-enhancement details
visualSuggestion: Abscess with surrounding edema

label: Cerebral edema
recognitionCue: T2 hyperintensity / increased water signal
structureMechanism: Excess tissue water
discriminator: MRI T2 is specifically sensitive to edema
visualSuggestion: T1 dark CSF vs T2 bright water

label: Neural tube defect due to folate deficiency
recognitionCue: Prenatal/open neural-tube abnormality; subtype determines appearance
structureMechanism: Inadequate folate impairs cell turnover during neural-tube closure
discriminator: Umbrella mechanism; name the specific defect from anatomy
visualSuggestion: Neural plate -> folds -> closure sites

label: Spina bifida occulta
recognitionCue: Closed skin over one or more unclosed vertebral arches; no meninges/cord involvement
structureMechanism: Failure of vertebral canal closure
discriminator: Skin closed; no protruding sac
visualSuggestion: Vertebral arch gap with intact skin

label: Meningocele
recognitionCue: Cystic protrusion containing meninges only
structureMechanism: Open vertebral defect permits meningeal herniation
discriminator: No cord in sac
visualSuggestion: Cross-section labeling sac contents

label: Myelomeningocele (meningomyelocele)
recognitionCue: Open spinal sac containing meninges and spinal cord
structureMechanism: Neural/vertebral closure failure with cord herniation
discriminator: Neural tissue inside sac
visualSuggestion: Side-by-side occulta, meningocele, myelomeningocele

label: Syringomyelia
recognitionCue: Segmental/bilateral loss of pain and temperature
structureMechanism: CSF-filled cavity near central canal damages crossing spinothalamic fibers
discriminator: Dissociated pain-temperature loss at affected segments
visualSuggestion: Cord cross-section with central cavity and crossing fibers

label: Tethered cord syndrome
recognitionCue: Low cord anchored to sacrum; symptoms not specified in deck
structureMechanism: Abnormal fixation limits normal cord movement/stretching
discriminator: Anatomic tethering rather than a free conus
visualSuggestion: Conus/filum anchored to sacrum

label: Encephalocele / cephalocele
recognitionCue: Cranial sac protruding through a skull defect
structureMechanism: Failure of portions of anterior neural tube to close
discriminator: Cranial herniation rather than spinal defect
visualSuggestion: Skull defect with meningeal/brain sac

label: Dandy-Walker syndrome/malformation
recognitionCue: Posterior fossa cyst with partial/complete vermian agenesis
structureMechanism: Congenital absence of Luschka and Magendie apertures -> cystic dilation communicating with fourth ventricle
discriminator: Vermis agenesis + enlarged cystic posterior fossa
visualSuggestion: Fourth ventricle, vermis, outlet foramina

label: Anencephaly
recognitionCue: Partial/complete absence of brain
structureMechanism: Failure of anterior neuropore closure
discriminator: Absent cranial vault/brain rather than focal encephalocele
visualSuggestion: Rostral neuropore failing to close

label: Multiple sclerosis
recognitionCue: CNS demyelinating deficits; detailed presentation not given here
structureMechanism: Oligodendrocytes/CNS myelin selectively affected
discriminator: CNS-side disease at the transition zone
visualSuggestion: Root transition with oligodendrocyte side highlighted

label: Guillain-Barre syndrome
recognitionCue: PNS demyelinating deficits; detailed presentation not given here
structureMechanism: Schwann cells/PNS myelin selectively affected
discriminator: PNS-side disease at the transition zone
visualSuggestion: Root transition with Schwann-cell side highlighted

label: Unilateral motor pathway lesion
recognitionCue: Weakness side depends on whether lesion is before or after pathway crossing
structureMechanism: CNS lesion before crossing -> contralateral weakness; after crossing or PNS lesion -> ipsilateral weakness
discriminator: Locate relative to decussation
visualSuggestion: Descending tract with crossing and five lesion points

label: Unilateral touch pathway lesion
recognitionCue: Loss of touch/vibration/proprioception with side determined by crossing
structureMechanism: CNS lesion after crossing -> contralateral loss; before crossing/PNS -> ipsilateral loss
discriminator: Dorsal-column crossing is in medulla
visualSuggestion: Ascending touch tract and medullary crossing

label: Unilateral pain pathway lesion
recognitionCue: Loss of pain with side determined by early spinal crossing
structureMechanism: CNS lesion after crossing -> contralateral loss; before crossing/PNS -> ipsilateral loss
discriminator: Pain crosses near entry in spinal cord
visualSuggestion: Spinothalamic crossing at segment

label: Epidural hemorrhage
recognitionCue: Trauma, fracture, rapid mass effect; biconvex/lenticular hematoma
structureMechanism: Usually middle meningeal artery rupture between skull and dura
discriminator: Lens-shaped and bounded by sutures
visualSuggestion: Skull -> epidural space -> dura

label: Subdural hemorrhage
recognitionCue: Trauma; chronic risk in older adults and neurodegenerative atrophy; crescent
structureMechanism: Bridging veins tear between subarachnoid space and dural sinus
discriminator: Crescent shape; venous source
visualSuggestion: Bridging veins stretched by atrophy

label: Subarachnoid hemorrhage
recognitionCue: Intense headache and stiff neck after trauma or spontaneous aneurysm rupture
structureMechanism: Cerebral artery bleeds into CSF-filled subarachnoid space
discriminator: Meningeal irritation + blood in cisterns/sulci
visualSuggestion: Artery in subarachnoid space leaking into CSF

label: Intracerebral hemorrhage
recognitionCue: Sudden focal deficit; deep basal ganglia/internal capsule injury can be devastating
structureMechanism: Intraparenchymal branches, especially lenticulostriate arteries, rupture
discriminator: Blood within brain substance; may enter ventricles
visualSuggestion: MCA -> lenticulostriates -> basal ganglia/internal capsule

label: Multiple sclerosis
recognitionCue: Blurred/partly lost vision, muscle weakness, incoordination
structureMechanism: Autoimmune CNS demyelination affects CN II, corticospinal tracts, cerebellar pathways
discriminator: CNS myelin + mixed optic/motor/cerebellar findings
visualSuggestion: Oligodendrocyte with plaques in three pathways

label: Guillain-Barre syndrome
recognitionCue: Symmetric ascending paralysis
structureMechanism: Inflammatory PNS demyelination affecting myelin and axons
discriminator: Ascending symmetric weakness; PNS, not CNS
visualSuggestion: Peripheral nerve myelin stripped distally-to-proximally

label: Tumors of glial origin
recognitionCue: Brain/spinal mass presentation not specified
structureMechanism: Neoplastic glial lineage; about half of brain tumors and one-quarter of spinal tumors per slide
discriminator: Do not infer a histologic subtype from this deck
visualSuggestion: Glial-cell family tree -> tumor

label: Gliosis
recognitionCue: Reactive change after CNS injury; presentation depends on the primary lesion
structureMechanism: Astrocytic/glial response to injury
discriminator: Reparative/reactive process rather than a glial neoplasm
visualSuggestion: Injury focus surrounded by reactive astrocytes
sourcePage: L05 objective p4; glial injury context p35-36

label: Axonal transection / Wallerian degeneration
recognitionCue: Traumatic nerve injury with distal degeneration
structureMechanism: Distal segment degenerates; Schwann cells guide PNS regeneration; CNS regeneration is poor
discriminator: PNS repair tube versus inhibitory/non-supportive CNS glia
visualSuggestion: Cut axon with proximal and distal responses

label: Pathologically elevated intracranial pressure
recognitionCue: Nausea, systemic hypertension, bradycardia, papilledema
structureMechanism: Increased intracranial volume/pressure
discriminator: Cushing-pattern hypertension + bradycardia with papilledema
visualSuggestion: Monro-Kellie compartments with pressure arrows

label: Noncommunicating (obstructive) hydrocephalus
recognitionCue: Infant: enlarged head, seizures, sleepiness, irritability, sun-setting eyes; older patient: headache, vomiting, gait/balance/cognitive/urinary problems
structureMechanism: Block within ventricular pathway at foramen of Monro, aqueduct, or fourth-ventricle outlets
discriminator: Ventricles enlarge upstream of obstruction
visualSuggestion: CSF flow map with three blockage sites

label: Pineal cyst/mass causing aqueductal obstruction
recognitionCue: Hydrocephalus with expanded upstream ventricles and bowed third-ventricle floor
structureMechanism: Pineal-region cyst prolapses into/blocks cerebral aqueduct
discriminator: Focal aqueduct blockage
visualSuggestion: Midline sagittal aqueduct and pineal mass

label: Hydrocephalus ex vacuo
recognitionCue: Enlarged ventricles in Alzheimer/Huntington neurodegeneration without a CSF-flow block
structureMechanism: Brain atrophy allows passive CSF space expansion
discriminator: Tissue loss, not pressure-driven obstruction
visualSuggestion: Normal brain versus atrophy with larger ventricles

label: Communicating hydrocephalus
recognitionCue: All ventricles enlarged; adult symptoms can overlap gait/cognitive/urinary dysfunction
structureMechanism: Impaired CSF absorption at arachnoid villi/superior sagittal sinus
discriminator: Dye can traverse ventricular system to lumbar CSF; no intraventricular block
visualSuggestion: CSF loop ending at arachnoid villi

label: Communicating hydrocephalus with normal ICP
recognitionCue: Mainly older adult; episodic ICP rise and ventricular expansion/distortion
structureMechanism: Communicating CSF imbalance with intermittently elevated pressure
discriminator: Measured pressure may be normal despite ventriculomegaly
visualSuggestion: Pressure-over-time curve with episodic spikes

label: Choroid plexus papilloma causing hydrocephalus
recognitionCue: Enlargement of all ventricles; other symptoms not specified
structureMechanism: Excess CSF secretion exceeds drainage
discriminator: Overproduction rather than impaired absorption
visualSuggestion: Choroid plexus tumor -> excess CSF

label: Vasogenic cerebral edema
recognitionCue: Often with tumor, abscess, trauma, hemorrhage; predominantly white matter
structureMechanism: BBB/capillary permeability increases -> extracellular plasma filtrate
discriminator: Extracellular, white matter, protein-containing fluid
visualSuggestion: Leaky capillary -> extracellular white-matter edema

label: Cytotoxic cerebral edema
recognitionCue: Often with hypoxia, ischemia, or water intoxication; gray and white matter
structureMechanism: ATP failure collapses ion gradients -> intracellular Na+/water swelling with intact BBB
discriminator: Intracellular swelling and intact BBB
visualSuggestion: Na/K pump failure -> swollen neuron/glia

label: Multiple sclerosis
recognitionCue: Multifocal CNS deficits with slowed/blocked conduction
structureMechanism: Autoimmune destruction of existing CNS myelin (myelinoclastic)
discriminator: CNS myelin destruction, not failed production
visualSuggestion: Myelinated CNS axon with plaques and conduction block

label: Vitamin B12-related CNS neuropathy / leukodystrophic pattern
recognitionCue: Sensory/ataxic or corticospinal findings; slide only identifies B12 deficiency as a cause
structureMechanism: Myelin is not properly produced
discriminator: Production failure rather than autoimmune myelin destruction
visualSuggestion: Normal myelin synthesis versus deficient wrapping

label: Guillain-Barre syndrome
recognitionCue: Weakness, loss of muscle control, ataxia, sensory loss/paresthesias; abnormal reflex/nerve-conduction testing
structureMechanism: Autoimmune Schwann-cell/PNS demyelination
discriminator: Acute PNS pattern versus CNS plaques
visualSuggestion: Peripheral myelin damage and slowed conduction trace

label: Chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy
recognitionCue: Similar weakness/sensory/ataxic PNS pattern; chronicity is the key inferred distinction
structureMechanism: Autoimmune Schwann-cell/PNS demyelination
discriminator: Chronic course versus acute GBS
visualSuggestion: Time course: acute GBS vs chronic CIDP

label: Seizure disorder treated by NaV-inactivating drugs
recognitionCue: Recurrent hyperexcitable firing; lecture focuses on therapy rather than syndrome
structureMechanism: Drug stabilizes inactive voltage-gated Na+ channels, preferentially suppressing firing/depolarized cells
discriminator: Use-dependent blockade of rapid trains
visualSuggestion: NaV states with drug bound to inactive state

label: Botulism / botulinum toxin effect
recognitionCue: Diplopia, dysphagia, xerostomia, dysarthria, descending/generalized weakness with possible respiratory paralysis
structureMechanism: Toxin cleaves synaptobrevin -> no ACh vesicle docking/release
discriminator: Flaccid weakness plus cranial/autonomic features; presynaptic ACh release failure
visualSuggestion: SNARE/synaptobrevin cut at NMJ

label: Dystonia treated with botulinum toxin
recognitionCue: Sustained abnormal muscle contraction/posture; deck names dystonia as a therapeutic use
structureMechanism: Local botulinum toxin reduces ACh release into the injected muscle
discriminator: Focal therapeutic chemodenervation rather than systemic botulism
visualSuggestion: Injected motor end plate with reduced ACh

label: Tetanus
recognitionCue: Infected wound followed by sustained powerful contractions/hypertonia
structureMechanism: Toxin degrades synaptobrevin in inhibitory interneurons -> blocks glycine/GABA release -> motor-neuron disinhibition
discriminator: Spastic contraction, unlike botulinum flaccid paralysis
visualSuggestion: Inhibitory interneuron blocked upstream of motor neuron

label: Beta-bungarotoxin envenomation
recognitionCue: Paralysis after snake venom exposure
structureMechanism: Binds actin cytoskeleton and inhibits synapsin-1 phosphorylation -> no vesicle release
discriminator: Venom exposure; presynaptic vesicle-release blockade
visualSuggestion: Synapsin/actin-vesicle diagram

label: Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome
recognitionCue: Proximal muscle weakness that briefly improves with sustained/repeated effort; associated with small-cell lung carcinoma
structureMechanism: Autoantibodies compromise presynaptic voltage-gated Ca2+ channels -> reduced ACh release
discriminator: Facilitation with repeated effort; presynaptic Ca2+ channel target
visualSuggestion: Nerve terminal Ca2+ channel with antibody and 4-AP effect

label: Small-cell lung carcinoma associated with Lambert-Eaton
recognitionCue: Smoker/cancer context plus facilitating weakness
structureMechanism: Paraneoplastic autoimmunity against presynaptic Ca2+ channels
discriminator: Cancer association supports Lambert-Eaton over myasthenia gravis
visualSuggestion: Lung tumor -> antibody -> NMJ

label: Cholinesterase inhibitor / organophosphate exposure
recognitionCue: Cholinergic excess; deck names neostigmine, physostigmine, sarin, tabun
structureMechanism: AChE blockade increases quantal size/prolongs ACh
discriminator: Excess ACh rather than failure of release
visualSuggestion: Synaptic cleft with blocked AChE

label: Tetrodotoxin/saxitoxin poisoning
recognitionCue: Paralysis/neurologic dysfunction
structureMechanism: Blocks voltage-gated Na+ channels -> blocks action potentials
discriminator: Conduction failure before synaptic release
visualSuggestion: Axon NaV channel blocked

label: Omega-conotoxin effect
recognitionCue: Weakness/paralysis
structureMechanism: Blocks presynaptic voltage-gated Ca2+ channels -> reduced quantal content
discriminator: Ca2+ entry failure at terminal
visualSuggestion: Presynaptic Ca2+ channel blockade

label: Alzheimer disease
recognitionCue: Progressive cognitive decline; lecture emphasizes basal forebrain cholinergic loss
structureMechanism: Nucleus basalis of Meynert degenerates -> reduced ACh
discriminator: AChE inhibitors are symptomatic, not disease-modifying
visualSuggestion: Nucleus basalis projections to cortex

label: Myasthenia gravis
recognitionCue: Fatigable skeletal weakness
structureMechanism: Disrupted cholinergic transmission at NMJ
discriminator: Postsynaptic NMJ disorder; improves pharmacologically with AChE inhibition
visualSuggestion: NMJ with fewer functional nicotinic receptors

label: Cholinergic overactivation (SLUD pattern)
recognitionCue: Salivation, lacrimation, urination, defecation
structureMechanism: Overactivation of muscarinic targets of postganglionic cholinergic fibers
discriminator: Wet muscarinic syndrome; treated with atropine
visualSuggestion: Four SLUD target organs around muscarinic receptor

label: Seizures from excitatory/inhibitory imbalance
recognitionCue: Synchronized hyperexcitable neuronal activity
structureMechanism: Increased glutamatergic drive and/or insufficient GABAergic restraint
discriminator: NMDA antagonism reduces Ca2+ entry; GABA agonism suppresses excitability
visualSuggestion: Balance scale: glutamate vs GABA

label: Upper motor neuron syndrome-associated weakness
recognitionCue: Weakness with UMN pattern
structureMechanism: Reduced glutamate release into bulbar/spinal motor nuclei per slide
discriminator: Central motor syndrome rather than NMJ/PNS weakness
visualSuggestion: Cortex -> bulbar/spinal motor nuclei

label: Anxiety
recognitionCue: Limbic hyperexcitability/altered excitability
structureMechanism: Benzodiazepines augment GABAergic transmission
discriminator: Limbic symptom context; GABA augmentation
visualSuggestion: Limbic neuron with GABA brake

label: Tetanus
recognitionCue: Sustained strong muscle contraction
structureMechanism: Toxin suppresses glycine release from bulbar/spinal interneurons -> LMN disinhibition
discriminator: Blocks transmitter release
visualSuggestion: Inhibitory interneuron terminal blocked

label: Strychnine poisoning
recognitionCue: Strong muscle contraction from motor-neuron disinhibition
structureMechanism: Blocks glycine receptor, reducing Cl- influx
discriminator: Blocks postsynaptic receptor, unlike tetanus release block
visualSuggestion: Tetanus at presynapse versus strychnine at receptor

label: Cocaine neurotoxicity
recognitionCue: Neurologic toxicity; specific presentation not detailed
structureMechanism: Dopaminergic/toxic mechanism not detailed on slide
discriminator: Keep as exposure association only
visualSuggestion: Dopamine synapse with cocaine label

label: Parkinsonism
recognitionCue: Decreased movement
structureMechanism: Dopamine deficiency/dysfunction; treated with dopamine agonist approach in slide
discriminator: Hypokinetic movement disorder
visualSuggestion: Nigrostriatal dopamine pathway

label: Psychosis
recognitionCue: Hallucinations and delusions
structureMechanism: Excess/abnormal dopamine signaling; antagonists used
discriminator: Positive psychotic symptoms rather than decreased movement
visualSuggestion: Dopamine high vs low comparison

label: Depression and pain
recognitionCue: Low mood and/or pain; slide focuses on treatment
structureMechanism: NE or serotonin reuptake/MAO inhibition activates descending opioidergic systems and suppresses substance P release
discriminator: Monoamine-linked descending analgesia
visualSuggestion: Brainstem monoamine -> dorsal horn substance P

label: Orthostatic hypotension in Parkinson disease
recognitionCue: Blood pressure drop on standing
structureMechanism: Loss of peripheral sympathetic neurons -> sympathetic insufficiency
discriminator: Autonomic symptom in Parkinson context
visualSuggestion: Standing BP arrow plus sympathetic neuron loss

lectureTitle: General Concepts of Cranial Nerves and Relationship to Skull
label: Pterion fracture with middle meningeal bleeding
recognitionCue: Lateral skull trauma followed by intracranial bleeding
structureMechanism: Thin pterion overlies middle meningeal artery; fracture can tear it
discriminator: Pterion = frontal/parietal/sphenoid/temporal junction
visualSuggestion: Four bones around pterion with artery deep to it

label: Deep neck infection spreading to mediastinum
recognitionCue: Neck infection with descending chest/mediastinal involvement
structureMechanism: Retropharyngeal/danger spaces act as conduits from neck to mediastinum
discriminator: Spread follows fascial planes rather than remaining superficial
visualSuggestion: Sagittal neck fascial spaces continuing into thorax

label: Facial palsy from parotid pathology/trauma
recognitionCue: Ipsilateral facial-expression weakness after parotid disease, trauma, or surgery
structureMechanism: CN VII branches traverse parotid gland and can be injured
discriminator: Motor deficit from intraparotid nerve injury; gland is not innervated by CN VII
visualSuggestion: Parotid contents ordered nerve-vein-artery

label: Parotid gland tumor
recognitionCue: Usually superficial parotid mass; detailed malignant signs not specified
structureMechanism: Neoplasm in superficial gland; may threaten CN VII
discriminator: Solid gland mass versus duct stone/inflammation
visualSuggestion: Parotid gland with superficial mass and CN VII

label: Parotid sialolithiasis
recognitionCue: Intense pain reproducible by salivary stimulation (for example lemon juice)
structureMechanism: Stone usually in main parotid duct obstructs flow
discriminator: Meal/sialagogue-related pain
visualSuggestion: Stensen duct with obstructing stone

label: Parotitis
recognitionCue: Painful enlarged/swollen gland, dry mouth, sometimes fever
structureMechanism: Duct obstruction or inflammatory disease
discriminator: Diffuse inflamed gland rather than focal duct stone/mass
visualSuggestion: Swollen parotid and dilated duct

label: Auriculotemporal (Frey) syndrome
recognitionCue: Gustatory facial sweating after parotidectomy
structureMechanism: Regenerating postganglionic parasympathetic fibers aberrantly synapse on sympathetic cholinergic sweat glands
discriminator: Sweating triggered by smell/eating after parotid surgery
visualSuggestion: Miswired parasympathetic axon to sweat gland

label: Trigeminal neuralgia
recognitionCue: Seconds-to-2-minute recurrent unilateral electric/severe facial pain, often V2/V3; facial spasm may accompany pain
structureMechanism: Often vascular compression of CN V near pons
discriminator: Brief paroxysms with triggers, not continuous aching
visualSuggestion: Pons, trigeminal root, compressing vessel, V2/V3 map

label: Facial infection spreading to cavernous sinus
recognitionCue: Infection in upper-lip-to-lower-eyelid triangle followed by orbital/CN signs
structureMechanism: Valveless facial, ophthalmic, pterygoid venous connections carry infection intracranially
discriminator: Location in facial danger triangle + cavernous-sinus pathway
visualSuggestion: Facial vein -> ophthalmic vein -> cavernous sinus

label: Scalp infection spreading intracranially
recognitionCue: Infection in loose areolar scalp layer
structureMechanism: Emissary veins connect danger layer to intracranial venous system
discriminator: Scalp danger layer rather than facial danger triangle
visualSuggestion: SCALP layers with emissary vein

label: Profusely bleeding scalp laceration
recognitionCue: Scalp wound with unexpectedly heavy bleeding
structureMechanism: Dense connective tissue holds cut vessels open so they cannot retract
discriminator: Heavy external bleeding from fixed-open vessels
visualSuggestion: Cross-section of vessel tethered in dense CT

label: Caput succedaneum
recognitionCue: Soft superficial swelling present at birth
structureMechanism: Fluid accumulates just beneath skin
discriminator: Crosses sutures and is immediately visible; more superficial than hemorrhages
visualSuggestion: Scalp layers with superficial fluid

label: Subgaleal hemorrhage
recognitionCue: Diffuse scalp swelling developing hours after delivery; can hold a large blood volume
structureMechanism: Bleeding between aponeurosis and periosteum
discriminator: Wide potential space and delayed enlargement
visualSuggestion: Galea-periosteum space spanning sutures

label: Cephalohematoma
recognitionCue: Localized swelling appearing 24-72 hours after delivery and resolving over weeks
structureMechanism: Bleeding between periosteum and bone
discriminator: Does not cross sutures
visualSuggestion: Periosteal bleed bounded by sutures

label: Trigeminal herpes zoster (shingles)
recognitionCue: Usually unilateral dermatomal vesicular rash; may cause toothache, neuralgia, blindness, encephalitis
structureMechanism: Latent VZV in trigeminal ganglion reactivates and travels along affected division
discriminator: Dermatomal unilateral vesicles; ocular involvement can threaten vision
visualSuggestion: Trigeminal ganglion with V1/V2/V3 dermatomes

label: Facial nerve lower motor lesion by level
recognitionCue: Ipsilateral facial weakness plus varying loss of taste/salivation/lacrimation depending on lesion location
structureMechanism: More proximal CN VII lesions interrupt more branch functions
discriminator: Use associated taste/gland deficits to localize along facial canal
visualSuggestion: CN VII course with branch-off points numbered

label: Bell palsy / peripheral facial palsy
recognitionCue: Complete ipsilateral upper and lower facial weakness
structureMechanism: CN VII injury from infection, trauma, surgery, or tumor
discriminator: Inability to frown/close forehead distinguishes LMN from cortical UMN pattern
visualSuggestion: Bilateral cortical input to upper face vs unilateral lower face

label: Cortical UMN facial lesion
recognitionCue: Contralateral lower-face weakness with forehead sparing
structureMechanism: Bilateral cortical innervation preserves upper facial movement
discriminator: “Upper spares upper”: forehead spared
visualSuggestion: Corticobulbar projections to upper/lower facial nuclei

label: Temporomandibular joint disorder/pain
recognitionCue: Jaw/TMJ tenderness, painful chewing, ear/facial ache, or locking with limited opening/closing
structureMechanism: Disc displacement; rheumatoid, gouty, psoriatic, or other inflammatory arthritis; or fracture/dislocation
discriminator: Locking/clicking-mechanical jaw symptoms rather than trigeminal electric pain
visualSuggestion: TMJ disc in normal vs displaced position

label: Cavernous sinus thrombosis from infratemporal infection
recognitionCue: Infratemporal infection followed by orbital/CN deficits
structureMechanism: Pterygoid venous plexus communicates with cavernous sinus and transmits infection
discriminator: Source in infratemporal/dental region plus cavernous-sinus signs
visualSuggestion: IT fossa -> pterygoid plexus -> cavernous sinus

label: Anterior epistaxis
recognitionCue: Nosebleed arising from the anterior nasal septum
structureMechanism: Highly vascular anastomotic Kiesselbach/Little area
discriminator: Most common site of significant epistaxis; anterior septal source
visualSuggestion: Nasal septum with Kiesselbach plexus circled

label: Retropharyngeal infection/mass with mediastinal spread
recognitionCue: Dysphagia and dysarthria with a deep-neck process; may descend into mediastinum
structureMechanism: Loose connective tissue in retropharyngeal potential space permits spread
discriminator: Deep fascial-space route, not a superficial neck lesion
visualSuggestion: Buccopharyngeal fascia, prevertebral fascia, mediastinum

label: Internal laryngeal nerve lesion
recognitionCue: Anesthesia/loss of sensation above vocal folds; aspiration risk
structureMechanism: Internal branch of superior laryngeal nerve carries supraglottic sensation
discriminator: Sensory loss rather than isolated voice weakness
visualSuggestion: Superior laryngeal nerve splitting internal/external branches

label: External laryngeal nerve lesion
recognitionCue: Weak voice that tires easily
structureMechanism: Denervation of cricothyroid impairs pitch/tension
discriminator: Voice fatigue/reduced high pitch rather than aphonia
visualSuggestion: Cricothyroid and external laryngeal nerve

label: Recurrent laryngeal nerve lesion
recognitionCue: Unilateral dysphonia; bilateral aphonia
structureMechanism: Denervation of intrinsic laryngeal muscles except cricothyroid
discriminator: Bilateral injury much more severe; cricothyroid spared
visualSuggestion: Recurrent nerve ascending beside tracheoesophageal groove

label: Acute upper-airway obstruction requiring cricothyroidotomy
recognitionCue: Airway blocked above vocal folds
structureMechanism: Median cricothyroid ligament is perforated to bypass obstruction
discriminator: Emergency access through cricothyroid membrane
visualSuggestion: Larynx with membrane entry below thyroid cartilage

label: Glossopharyngeal nerve lesion
recognitionCue: Loss of posterior-third tongue taste/general sensation, oropharyngeal/tonsillar sensation, carotid body/sinus input, stylopharyngeus function, and possibly parotid secretion
structureMechanism: CN IX injury interrupts its sensory, motor, visceral sensory, and parasympathetic branches
discriminator: Posterior-third taste + absent afferent gag points to IX
visualSuggestion: CN IX branches to tongue, pharynx, carotid sinus, parotid

label: Glossopharyngeal neuralgia
recognitionCue: Seconds-to-minutes recurrent severe pain in tongue, throat, ear, tonsil triggered by swallowing, chewing, coughing, laughing, or speaking
structureMechanism: CN IX irritation, sometimes from neurovascular compression, skull-base tumor, or throat/mouth infection
discriminator: Triggered throat/ear pain rather than V2/V3 facial pain
visualSuggestion: CN IX sensory territories with compressing vessel

label: Vagus nerve lesion
recognitionCue: Dysphagia/voice/laryngeal sensory-motor deficits depending on branch level
structureMechanism: CN X injury interrupts pharyngeal plexus and/or laryngeal branches
discriminator: Palatal/laryngeal findings plus efferent gag/cough dysfunction
visualSuggestion: CN X branching to pharynx and larynx

label: Internal laryngeal nerve palsy
recognitionCue: Dysphagia, odynophagia, foreign-body sensation
structureMechanism: Loss of supraglottic sensory/secretomotor innervation; often surgical
discriminator: Predominantly sensory swallowing complaint
visualSuggestion: Internal laryngeal sensory field above glottis

label: External laryngeal nerve palsy
recognitionCue: Reduced high-pitch voice, fatigue, poor volume/projection
structureMechanism: Cricothyroid denervation; often after thyroid/parathyroid surgery
discriminator: Cannot sustain/raise pitch, but not the classic RLN hoarseness pattern
visualSuggestion: Cricothyroid tensioning vocal fold

label: Recurrent laryngeal nerve palsy
recognitionCue: Unilateral new hoarseness/noisy breathing; bilateral severe breathing and swallowing difficulty
structureMechanism: Injury from thyroid/parathyroid surgery, tumor, intubation, or viral illness denervates most intrinsic laryngeal muscles
discriminator: Hoarseness/airway compromise; cricothyroid remains intact
visualSuggestion: RLN route and unilateral vs bilateral cord positions

label: Absent gag reflex from CN IX injury
recognitionCue: No reflex after touching posterior pharynx/tonsil/base of tongue
structureMechanism: Afferent limb IX fails; efferent bilateral pharyngeal contraction is X
discriminator: Separate afferent IX from efferent X
visualSuggestion: Two-limb reflex arc

label: Impaired cough reflex / aspiration risk
recognitionCue: Poor clearance of secretions/foreign bodies and aspiration risk
structureMechanism: CN X afferent from upper airway/diaphragm and CN X-linked brainstem motor output coordinate cough
discriminator: Gag tests pharyngeal arc; cough tests airway-protective arc
visualSuggestion: Inspiratory -> compression -> expiratory phases

label: Hypoglossal nerve injury
recognitionCue: On protrusion, tongue deviates toward the weak side; acute ipsilateral paralysis, chronic atrophy; posterior fall can obstruct airway
structureMechanism: CN XII denervates ipsilateral tongue muscles, especially genioglossus action
discriminator: LMN XII lesion: atrophy and deviation toward lesion
visualSuggestion: Paired genioglossus vectors with one side off

label: Dysphagia assessed by videofluoroscopy
recognitionCue: Difficulty swallowing visualized during oral transit; deck supplies image/technique but no specific cause
structureMechanism: Oral/pharyngeal transit dysfunction
discriminator: Functional moving swallow study rather than static anatomy
visualSuggestion: Bolus path across sequential swallow frames

lectureTitle: Gross Anatomy of the Orbit and Eye
label: Cavernous-sinus inflammation/infection injuring ocular cranial nerves
recognitionCue: Orbital/eye-movement deficits after extracranial facial/orbital infection
structureMechanism: Valveless ophthalmic/pterygoid veins transmit infection; CN III, IV, V1, V2 lie in wall and CN VI/ICA traverse sinus
discriminator: Multiple ocular motor/sensory nerves affected together
visualSuggestion: Cavernous-sinus cross-section labeling ICA and CNs

lectureTitle: Gross Anatomy of the Orbit and Eye
label: CN III damage causing eye-movement deficit/diplopia
recognitionCue: Loss of several adduction/elevation/depression functions; exact resting-eye description not supplied
structureMechanism: CN III supplies MR, SR, IR, IO and levator
discriminator: No single movement fully defines III because multiple muscles cooperate; test muscles in isolated gaze
visualSuggestion: Six extraocular muscles with III/IV/VI labels

label: Chalazion
recognitionCue: Painless eyelid cyst
structureMechanism: Block/inflammation of a Meibomian/tarsal gland
discriminator: Painless deep lid nodule versus painful stye
visualSuggestion: Eyelid cross-section with tarsal gland

label: Stye (hordeolum)
recognitionCue: Painful, tender, red eyelid lesion
structureMechanism: Gland of Zeis lesion/infection
discriminator: Pain and lid-margin tenderness versus painless chalazion
visualSuggestion: Eyelash with Zeis gland

label: Conjunctivitis
recognitionCue: Redness, irritation, foreign-body sensation; watery/clear allergic discharge or opaque purulent bacterial discharge
structureMechanism: Inflamed palpebral and/or bulbar conjunctiva
discriminator: Discharge character helps classify; conjunctiva rather than deeper cornea/uvea
visualSuggestion: Palpebral, bulbar, fornix regions

label: Corneal disease requiring transplant
recognitionCue: Damaged/opaque cornea from keratitis, trauma, keratoconus, or degeneration
structureMechanism: Diseased cornea replaced by donor tissue
discriminator: Corneal avascularity gives relatively low rejection response
visualSuggestion: Five corneal layers and graft depth options

label: Marfan syndrome with lens dislocation
recognitionCue: Lens displacement in a patient with fibrillin disorder
structureMechanism: Zonular fibers are primarily fibrillin; weakness permits lens dislocation
discriminator: Ectopia lentis linked to zonular-fiber defect
visualSuggestion: Ciliary process -> zonule -> lens

label: Glaucoma, especially acute angle-closure
recognitionCue: Eye pain, headache, vomiting, blurred/lost vision, halos; red edematous cornea, fixed mid-dilated pupil, reduced peripheral field, raised IOP
structureMechanism: Excess secretion or impaired aqueous drainage raises IOP -> ocular perfusion/optic-nerve damage
discriminator: Painful red eye + mid-dilated pupil + halos is acute angle-closure pattern
visualSuggestion: Aqueous flow and blocked iridocorneal angle

label: Cataract
recognitionCue: Progressive visual loss with cloudy lens
structureMechanism: Crystallin conformational change/cross-linking causes loss of lens transparency
discriminator: Lens opacity without the painful high-IOP pattern
visualSuggestion: Clear lens beside opaque lens

label: Night blindness
recognitionCue: Poor vision in low light
structureMechanism: Rod dysfunction/deficiency; rods carry rhodopsin and dominate low-light vision
discriminator: Night/dusk deficit, not color discrimination
visualSuggestion: Rod-rich peripheral retina

label: Color blindness
recognitionCue: Impaired color discrimination
structureMechanism: Cone pigment/function abnormality
discriminator: Color deficit with preserved rod-mediated night vision
visualSuggestion: Three cone types and wavelengths

label: Optic neuritis in multiple sclerosis
recognitionCue: Visual loss/blur with optic-nerve inflammation
structureMechanism: Demyelinating plaques affect optic nerve/chiasm
discriminator: Optic nerve demyelination rather than retinal-layer separation
visualSuggestion: Retina -> optic disc -> demyelinated optic nerve

label: Age-related macular degeneration
recognitionCue: Central visual loss/distortion
structureMechanism: Degeneration at macula/foveal region
discriminator: Central high-acuity loss; peripheral retina relatively spared
visualSuggestion: Macula/fovea centered on visual axis

label: Retinal detachment
recognitionCue: Floaters/“shower of paper,” flashes, and a veil/curtain over vision
structureMechanism: Neural retina separates from RPE, often at RPE-photoreceptor junction, depriving photoreceptors of choroidal nutrition
discriminator: Curtain/flash/floaters; risk after cataract surgery, trauma, dehydration, or tear
visualSuggestion: RPE, rods/cones, and detachment plane

label: Middle-ear infection spreading to mastoid or nasopharynx
recognitionCue: Otitis symptoms with mastoid involvement, or infection traversing the auditory-tube route
structureMechanism: Continuous mucosa links middle ear to mastoid air cells and pharyngotympanic tube/nasopharynx
discriminator: Track spread posteriorly to mastoid or anteriorly to nasopharynx
visualSuggestion: Middle ear with two arrows: mastoid and auditory tube

label: Perforated tympanic membrane
recognitionCue: Sudden ear pain, discharge, tinnitus, vertigo; temporary or permanent hearing loss
structureMechanism: Infection, trauma, or loud noise ruptures tympanic membrane, connecting external canal to middle ear
discriminator: Visible membrane rupture with acute symptoms
visualSuggestion: External canal -> torn membrane -> middle ear

label: Vertigo from excessive vestibular stimulation / motion sickness
recognitionCue: False spinning after rotation, or carsickness
structureMechanism: Excess semicircular-canal stimulation or utricular stimulation
discriminator: Provoked physiologically by spinning/linear motion
visualSuggestion: Canals for angular vs utricle for linear acceleration

label: Acoustic neuroma associated with vertigo
recognitionCue: Vertigo with tumor context; other classic features not specified in deck
structureMechanism: Tumor affects vestibular pathway
discriminator: Do not add unilateral hearing-loss details unless sourced elsewhere
visualSuggestion: CN VIII with vestibular tumor

label: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo
recognitionCue: Brief position-triggered vertigo
structureMechanism: Otoconia detach from utricle and lodge in a crista/semicircular canal, usually posterior, moving stereocilia inappropriately
discriminator: Positional episodes; displaced otoconia
visualSuggestion: Utricle otoconia falling into posterior canal

label: Meniere disease (endolymphatic hydrops)
recognitionCue: Episodic vertigo with hearing involvement
structureMechanism: Cochlear-aqueduct blockage -> increased endolymphatic pressure affecting balance and hearing
discriminator: Both vestibular and auditory symptoms
visualSuggestion: Membranous labyrinth distended with endolymph

label: Conductive hearing loss
recognitionCue: Sound is mechanically impeded before reaching inner-ear receptors
structureMechanism: Otitis media, excess cerumen, foreign body, or otosclerosis obstructs external/middle-ear transmission
discriminator: Mechanical pathway lesion; sensory receptors/nerve intact
visualSuggestion: Sound path with external/middle-ear block

label: Sensorineural hearing loss
recognitionCue: Hearing loss from receptor, nerve, or auditory-cortex injury
structureMechanism: Membranous-labyrinth infection, temporal-bone fracture, acoustic trauma, or aging damages sensory/neural pathway
discriminator: Inner-ear/neural lesion rather than mechanical impedance
visualSuggestion: Cochlea/organ of Corti -> CN VIII -> cortex

label: Presbycusis
recognitionCue: Age-related high-frequency hearing loss
structureMechanism: Sensory-cell loss begins at basal end of cochlea
discriminator: High frequencies lost first; aging context
visualSuggestion: Cochlear tonotopy with basal high-frequency loss

label: Otosclerosis
recognitionCue: Progressive conductive hearing loss
structureMechanism: Ossicular/stapes fixation impedes mechanical transmission
discriminator: Conductive category despite intact cochlear receptors
visualSuggestion: Stapes fixed at oval window

label: Acoustic trauma
recognitionCue: Hearing loss after prolonged excessive noise
structureMechanism: Sensory hair-cell injury
discriminator: Exposure history + sensorineural category
visualSuggestion: Basilar membrane/organ of Corti hair-cell damage
